docs.title: 5.4 How the folds give train, validation and test
docs.text:
There is no single fixed train / validation / test split. The folds take turns, as in the PASTIS benchmark (Garnot & Landrieu 2021): in each of 5 rounds, 3 folds train, the next fold validates (chooses the hyperparameters) and one fold is the test fold.

Round Train Validation Test 1 folds 2, 3, 4 fold 1 fold 0 2 folds 3, 4, 0 fold 2 fold 1 3 folds 4, 0, 1 fold 3 fold 2 4 folds 0, 1, 2 fold 4 fold 3 5 folds 1, 2, 3 fold 0 fold 4

After 5 rounds every parcel has been tested once, by a model that never saw its block. Unlike PASTIS, the folds are made of whole 20 km blocks, so the test fold is always a set of regions the model has never seen.

For quick experiments, the column split gives one fixed split: fold 0 = test, fold 1 = validation, folds 2–4 = train. random_fold gives a stratified random split, so the optimism of random validation can be measured.

Outputs (outputs/morocco/dataset/02_folds/): - parcels_folds.geojson: parcels + block_id, fold, random_fold, split - fold_counts.csv - block_size_comparison.csv - class_similarity_by_distance.csv / .png - leakage_check.csv - spatial_folds.png, spatial_folds_blocks.png - train_test_distance.png

docs.title: 6. Script 03 — build_tiles
docs.text: Purpose: build the single image store that every model reads from.

docs.title: 6.1 Tile grid and which tiles are built
docs.text:
• One projection for the whole area, UTM 29N (EPSG:32629), with 10 m pixels. The few parcels in zone 30N are resampled.
  • A fixed grid of 128 × 128-pixel tiles (1.28 km × 1.28 km). Tile IDs are <season>_<ix>_<iy>, e.g. 2023-24_412_3561.
  • Only the tiles the parcels need are built:
  • home tile: holds the parcel centroid;
  • outline tiles: touched by the parcel polygon;
  • context tiles: reached by the largest model chip around the centroid. That is 64 px plus up to 8 px of alignment shift, i.e. 40 px (400 m) in every direction.
flowchart LR P["Parcel<br/>centroid + outline"] --> H["home tile<br/>(contains centroid)"] P --> O["outline tiles<br/>(polygon crosses into them)"] P --> C["context tiles<br/>(within 32 + 8 px of the centroid)"] H --> U["Union over all parcels<br/>and both seasons"] O --> U C --> U U --> T["Tile plan:<br/>each tile built once"]

docs.title: 6.2 Two agricultural years
docs.text:
The survey ran from December 2023 to January 2025, so the parcels belong to two agricultural years. Each parcel must be described by the imagery of the season in which its label was observed. A field that was irrigated in 2023/24 may be rainfed or fallow in 2024/25. The two years are therefore handled as two separate, parallel tile stores that share one grid:

flowchart TD A["Survey date of each parcel"] --> B["<b>ag_season</b> = agricultural year (1 Sep – 31 Aug)<br/>Sep–Dec of Y → Y/Y+1 · Jan–Aug of Y → Y−1/Y"] B --> P1["<b>2023/24</b> · 6,887 parcels<br/>tile plan: tile_id = 2023-24_ix_iy"] B --> P2["<b>2024/25</b> · 1,894 parcels<br/>tile plan: tile_id = 2024-25_ix_iy"] P1 --> X1["Label rasters: only 2023/24 parcels<br/>Earth Engine image Sep 2023 – Aug 2024<br/>(2023/24 tiles + 2 km)"] P2 --> X2["Label rasters: only 2024/25 parcels<br/>Earth Engine image Sep 2024 – Aug 2025<br/>(2024/25 tiles + 2 km)"] X1 --> T1["2,183 tiles (2023/24)"] X2 --> T2["804 tiles (2024/25)"] T1 --> S["One folder tiles/, one grid (same ix, iy),<br/>season in every tile name"] T2 --> S S --> V["04_make_views.py reads each parcel<br/>from the tiles of its own season"]

How each part of the pipeline handles the season:

Where How the season is handled 01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py ag_season from the survey date: 1 Sep – 31 Aug (a parcel surveyed in Jan 2024 → 2023/24; Dec 2024 → 2024/25) Tile plan a tile is the triple (season, ix, iy). The same 1.28 km square can exist once for each year, with the same grid position. Tile name the season comes first: 2023-24_374_2793, 2024-25_374_2793 Label rasters only parcels of the tile's own year are burnt in, so a 2024/25 parcel never appears as a label in a 2023/24 tile Imagery one 12-month Earth Engine image per year, built over that year's tiles only. The month bands are named identically (m01 … m12), so both years have the same 228-band layout and models can mix them. QA, tiles.parquet one row per (season, tile), with an ag_season column Views (04_make_views.py) every parcel is cut from the tiles of its own season; ag_season is kept in every output table Folds (02) blocks are defined by location only, so a place surveyed in both years falls in the same block and fold. No information leaks between years from training to test. Viewing (tools/a4_build_vrt.py) one virtual raster per year, because the two years overlap in space

Currently 47 tile positions exist in both years: places with parcels surveyed in 2023/24 and in 2024/25.

Why the agricultural year (September – August).

gantt dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD axisFormat %b section Rainfed cereals Pre-season :r0, 2023-09-01, 2023-11-01 Sowing :r1, 2023-11-01, 2024-01-01 Growth, flowering Mar–Apr :r2, 2024-01-01, 2024-05-01 Harvest :r3, 2024-05-01, 2024-07-31 section Irrigated land Green whenever water is applied :i1, 2023-09-01, 2024-06-01 Dry summer :crit, i2, 2024-06-01, 2024-08-31 Reason Explanation One complete rainfed cycle rainfed cereals are sown in November–December and harvested in May–July; a calendar year would divide the cycle The dry summer carries the signal from June to August only irrigated fields remain green, the clearest contrast between the classes (confirmed by the permutation importance in E01) Irrigation status is seasonal rainfall, reservoir allocations and fallowing change which fields are irrigated, so a label is valid for one season Consistency with existing products LGRIP30, WorldCereal and GMIA-NEXT define irrigation for one growing season (Teluguntla et al., 2023; Van Tricht et al., 2023; Kebede et al., 2026) National convention the Moroccan agricultural campaign, including the accounting of seasonal rainfall, starts on 1 September

docs.title: 6.3 Monthly composites (per tile, per month)
docs.text:
flowchart TD subgraph S2["Sentinel-2 L2A"] direction TB A1["Scenes with cloud cover < 60 %"] --> A2["Cloud Score+ mask:<br/>keep pixels with cs_cdf ≥ 0.60"] A2 --> A3["Median of clear pixels<br/>12 bands, reflectance × 10,000"] A3 --> A4["+ S2_NCLEAR: number of<br/>clear observations"] end subgraph S1["Sentinel-1 GRD (IW, VV + VH)"] direction TB B1["Split by orbit:<br/>ascending / descending"] --> B2["dB → linear power;<br/>monthly mean"] B2 --> B3["→ dB × 100<br/>VV, VH per orbit"] B3 --> B4["+ S1_N: number of scenes"] end A4 --> M["One month = 19 bands"] B4 --> M M --> Y["12 months (Sep → Aug) = 228 bands, int16<br/>NODATA = −32768 where no observation"]
  • 19 bands per month:
  • B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B8A, B9, B11, B12
  • S2_NCLEAR
  • VV_ASC, VH_ASC, S1_N_ASC
  • VV_DSC, VH_DSC, S1_N_DSC
  • Months: m01 = September … m12 = August of the parcel's agricultural year. Band names in the GeoTIFF look like B4_m03 (red, November).
  • Why linear power for Sentinel-1: backscatter in dB is a logarithm. Averaging in dB gives the geometric mean and biases the composite downwards. Averaging is therefore done in linear power, and the result converted back to dB.
  • Why the orbits are kept apart: ascending and descending passes look at a field from different incidence angles, so their backscatter is not interchangeable. Both are stored, and the view script picks one.
  • Each tile's _scenes.json lists the Sentinel-1/2 scene IDs used in each month, so every pixel can be traced to its source.

docs.title: 6.4 Label rasters (local, no Earth Engine)
docs.text:
Each tile has a 3-band int32 label raster on exactly the same grid:

Band Values Meaning label 0 / 1 / 2 0 = unlabelled or ignore, 1 = irrigated, 2 = rainfed parcel_idx 0 / 1…N 0 = no parcel, otherwise the parcel's row in parcels.csv edge 0 / 1 1 = parcel pixel within 10 m of the outline (mixed boundary pixel)

Rules:

flowchart TD A["Parcel polygon<br/>(same season as the tile)"] --> B{"Contains at least<br/>one pixel centre?"} B -->|yes| C["Burn pixels whose<br/>centre is inside"] B -->|no: very small parcel| D["Burn all touched pixels<br/>flag all_touched = True"] C --> E{"Pixel claimed by<br/>two parcels?"} D --> E E -->|yes| F["label = 0, parcel_idx = 0<br/>(ignore) · pair listed in parcel_overlaps.csv"] E -->|no| G["label, parcel_idx set"] G --> H["edge = 1 if within 10 m<br/>of the outline"]

Only parcels of the tile's own agricultural year are burnt in.

docs.title: 6.5 Steps
docs.text:
1. Read the parcels with folds and project them to UTM 29N.
  2. Parcel table: index, centroid, bounds, area, perimeter, pixel counts (all and inner), home tile, tiles needed.
  3. Tile plan (6.1).
  4. Label rasters for all planned tiles (6.3). Local and fast.
  5. Earth Engine: one 228-band monthly image per agricultural year. Each tile is downloaded with computePixels, 8 requests in parallel and up to 4 retries, and written as a compressed GeoTIFF with its scene IDs. Finished tiles are skipped on a restart.
  6. Tile index (tiles.parquet) with fold, role, labelled pixels and QA.

DOWNLOAD = False stops after step 4, so the plan and labels can be checked without Earth Engine. N_TEST_TILES = 20 builds only 20 tiles per season, for a test run.

docs.title: 6.6 Quality numbers per tile
docs.text:
Column Meaning s2_nodata_pct share of tile-months without any clear Sentinel-2 pixel s2_nodata_parcel_pct the same, on parcel pixels only s2_nclear_parcel_median median number of clear observations on parcel pixels, per month s1_asc_months, s1_dsc_months months with at least one ascending / descending scene role home, outline or context mixed_folds the tile holds parcels from more than one fold (relevant for segmentation, section 11)

Outputs (outputs/morocco/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/): - tiles/<id>_img.tif, tiles/<id>_lab.tif, tiles/<id>_scenes.json - parcels.csv - parcel_overlaps.csv - tiles.parquet - tiles_qa.jsonl - tiles_info.json

docs.title: 6.7 Visual check of tiles — 03b_tile_quicklooks.py
docs.text:
03b_tile_quicklooks.py draws one figure per tile for a visual check of the tile store: the 12 monthly composites as true colour (B4/B3/B2), NDVI and Sentinel-1 VH, the three label rasters (label, parcel index, edge pixels) and the mean NDVI and VH per month of the irrigated and rainfed parcel pixels. By default it selects, per agricultural year, the three downloaded home tiles with the most pixels of both classes, the tile with the most irrigated pixels and the tile with the most rainfed pixels (Sentinel-2 missing data < 1 %); TILE_IDS selects tiles explicitly. The Sentinel-1 orbit with more observations in the tile is drawn (ORBIT = "auto"). The region is set with REGION at the top, as in scripts 02–04.

Output: outputs/<region>/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/quicklooks/<tile_id>.png

docs.title: 7. Script 04 — make_views
docs.text:
Purpose: cut every model input from the tile store. It runs locally and needs no Earth Engine.

flowchart TD TS["<b>Tile store</b><br/>tiles read through a cache of 48 tiles"] --> L["<b>For each parcel</b><br/>read its window and its pixels<br/>(label raster: parcel_idx = this parcel)"] L --> A["<b>View A · parcel features</b><br/>median per band and month + NDVI, NDWI, EVI<br/>parcel_features_all.csv · parcel_features_inner.csv"] L --> B["<b>View B · pixel sets</b><br/>all parcel pixels, all months<br/>pixelsets.npz"] L --> C["<b>View C · 64 × 64 chips</b><br/>patch-aligned, per patch size<br/>chips_p8/ (Clay) · chips_p16/ (others)"] TS --> D["<b>View D · full tiles</b><br/>as they are, for<br/>segmentation models"]

docs.title: 7.1 View A — parcel feature tables
docs.text:
• Per parcel and month: the median over the parcel's pixels of each of these:
  • the 12 Sentinel-2 bands (reflectance 0–1);
  • NDVI = (B8 − B4)/(B8 + B4);
  • NDWI = (B8 − B11)/(B8 + B11), which measures canopy water;
  • EVI = 2.5 (B8 − B4)/(B8 + 6 B4 − 7.5 B2 + 1);
  • VV and VH for both orbits (dB).
  • Indices are computed per pixel first, then the median is taken.
  • The median is used instead of the mean because it is robust to leftover clouds and mixed edge pixels.
  • Observation counts are added: the mean S2_NCLEAR over the parcel, and the maximum S1_N per orbit.
  • Column names are <variable>_m<month>, e.g. NDVI_m10 (NDVI in June). Each parcel has 19 variables × 12 months = 228 feature columns, plus counts and metadata (parcel_id, label, ag_season, fold, n_px_used, used_inner).
  • parcel_features_inner.csv leaves out edge pixels. A parcel with no inner pixel falls back to all of its pixels (used_inner = False).

docs.title: 7.2 View B — pixel sets
docs.text:
All pixels of each parcel, unaggregated, for set-based temporal models such as PSE-TAE (Garnot et al. 2020).

  • pixels [N_pixels, 12, bands] int16
  • offsets [parcels + 1]: parcel i = pixels[offsets[i]:offsets[i+1]]
  • edge [N_pixels], parcel_id, label, bands

docs.title: 7.3 View C — patch-aligned chips for the foundation models
docs.text:
Vision-transformer foundation models partition an image into square patches: 8 × 8 px for Clay and 16 × 16 px (160 m) for Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind and the output grid of AgriFM. Each patch is represented by one embedding.

When a chip whose size is a multiple of the patch size is centred on the parcel, the centroid falls on the corner of four patches, and a small parcel is distributed over four patches dominated by neighbouring fields. Shifting the chip by half a patch places the centroid at the centre of a single patch:

flowchart LR subgraph OLD["Centred chip (old)"] O1["Centroid on the corner<br/>of 4 patches"] --> O2["Parcel split over 4 patches,<br/>each mostly neighbouring fields"] end subgraph NEW["Patch-aligned chip (now)"] N1["Chip shifted by half a patch<br/>(4 px for p8, 8 px for p16)"] --> N2["Centroid at the centre<br/>of one patch"] N2 --> N3["Higher share of the pooled<br/>patches inside the parcel"] end OLD -.->|"replaced by"| NEW

Purity measures this. A patch's weight is the share of its pixels inside the parcel, and those weights are also what the study uses to pool patch embeddings. Purity is the weighted share of parcel pixels in the pooled patches: Σ w² / Σ w, from 0 to 1. index.csv stores both purity (aligned) and purity_centred (old rule), so the gain is measurable.

Each chip folder holds: - part_*.npz: chips [n, 12, 15, 64, 64] int16, mask [n, 64, 64] (parcel pixels), parcel_id. - index.csv: one row per parcel. Columns: part, label, ag_season, fold, zone, lat, lon, epsg, x0, y0 (chip top-left corner, for georeferencing), area_ha, n_px, n_px_in_chip, purity, purity_centred. - chips_info.json: band order and scales. The 15 bands are B1 … B12, VV, VH, S2_NCLEAR.

Figure 1.10. Patch purity, i.e. the share of the pooled patches that lies inside the parcel, for centred chips (grey) and patch-aligned chips (blue), at 8 px (80 m, left) and 16 px (160 m, right) patch size. Alignment markedly increases purity, in particular for 8 px patches.

docs.title: 7.4 Sentinel-1 orbit for views B and C
docs.text: S1_ORBIT = "auto" picks the orbit direction with more valid tile-months over the whole study area and writes it to views_info.json (s1_orbit_for_chips_and_pixelsets). That orbit's bands are named simply VV and VH in the chips. "ASC" or "DSC" force one orbit. View A keeps both orbits as separate columns.

docs.title: 7.5 QA files
docs.text:
• qa_clear_obs.csv: clear observations per parcel and month.
  • qa_purity.csv: purity distribution per patch size.
  • views_info.json: settings, the chosen orbit, and counts.

docs.title: 7.6 Dataset inspection
docs.text:
The checks of models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py (Model training and inference §4) characterise the final dataset before any model is trained.

Figure 1.11. Mean number of clear Sentinel-2 observations per parcel and month (left) and share of parcels without any clear observation (right). Winter months have the fewest clear views, yet every parcel has at least one clear observation in every month. Figure 1.12. Monthly parcel medians of NDVI, NDWI and Sentinel-1 VH backscatter (median and interquartile range per class). Irrigated parcels show markedly higher vegetation and moisture signals from December to April and higher backscatter throughout the year; rainfed parcels show a weak, short spring peak. Figure 1.13. Example irrigated parcels: 16 px-aligned chips for the 12 months of the agricultural year, in true colour and NDVI (outline = parcel). Figure 1.14. Example rainfed parcels, displayed as in Figure 1.13.

docs.title: 8. Output layout and file formats
docs.text:
outputs/morocco/dataset/
├── 01_labels/
│   ├── parcels_labelled.geojson         EPSG:4326 polygons
│   └── summary.csv, *.png
├── 02_folds/
│   ├── parcels_folds.geojson            + block_id, fold, random_fold, split
│   └── fold_counts.csv, block_size_comparison.csv, leakage_check.csv, class_similarity_by_distance.csv, *.png
└── 03_tiles_128px/agyear/
    ├── tiles/
    │   ├── <tile_id>_img.tif            int16, 228 bands (12 months × 19), NODATA −32768, EPSG:32629, 10 m
    │   ├── <tile_id>_lab.tif            int32, 3 bands: label, parcel_idx, edge
    │   └── <tile_id>_scenes.json        scene IDs per month (S2, S1 asc, S1 dsc)
    ├── parcels.csv                      one row per parcel (parcel_idx = value in the label raster)
    ├── parcel_overlaps.csv              overlapping parcel pairs, their labels and overlap share
    ├── tiles.parquet                    GeoParquet tile index: geometry, season, role, fold(s), QA
    ├── tiles_info.json                  grid, bands, months, scales, cloud settings
    └── views/
        ├── parcel_features_all.csv      view A
        ├── parcel_features_inner.csv    view A, edge pixels removed
        ├── pixelsets.npz                view B
        ├── chips_p8/  chips_p16/        view C: part_*.npz, index.csv, chips_info.json
        ├── qa_purity.csv, qa_clear_obs.csv
        └── views_info.json

Scales: - Sentinel-2: reflectance × 10,000. - Sentinel-1: dB × 100. For example, −1,523 = −15.23 dB. - Counts: plain integers. - −32,768 = no observation. Count bands are 0 there.

docs.title: 9. How to use the dataset
docs.text:
Model family Use Train / validation / test Random forest, gradient boosting, SVM View A fold (5 rounds: 3 train / 1 validation / 1 test) or split Pixel-set temporal models (PSE-TAE, L-TAE) View B same Foundation models / any CNN or ViT on chips View C (chips_p8 or chips_p16) with mask same, from index.csv Segmentation (U-Net, U-TAE) View D: _img.tif + _lab.tif, loss masked where label = 0 split by tile, using tiles.parquet (fold, mixed_folds)

Minimal example: read the chips.

import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
folder = "outputs/morocco/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/views/chips_p16"
index = pd.read_csv(f"{folder}/index.csv", dtype={"parcel_id": str})
info = json.load(open(f"{folder}/chips_info.json"))
d = np.load(f"{folder}/{index.part.iloc[0]}")
chips, mask = d["chips"], d["mask"]            # [n, 12, 15, 64, 64], [n, 64, 64]
red_june = chips[0, 9, info["bands"].index("B4")] / 10000

docs.title: 10. Running, settings and run time
docs.text:
conda activate condaml
python ml_dataset_prep/01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py   # minutes
python ml_dataset_prep/02_make_spatial_folds.py      # minutes
python ml_dataset_prep/03_build_tiles.py             # Earth Engine; a few hours; resumable
python ml_dataset_prep/04_make_views.py              # local

Scripts 02–04 serve both study regions: set REGION = "morocco" at the top of each (the default). The settings that differ between regions (projection, agricultural year, block size, map boundaries) are in ml_dataset_prep/regions.py; the Utah dataset is built the same way (Utah training data).

Run 03 first with N_TEST_TILES = 20, then check the result with models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py and tools/a3_export_chips_geotiff.py (QGIS) before the full run.

To view the whole tile store as one layer, tools/a4_build_vrt.py writes virtual rasters (one per agricultural year: labels, true / false colour and Sentinel-1 per month) to outputs/morocco/dataset/03_tiles_128px/agyear/vrt/. They only point to the tiles, so nothing is copied.

The settings sit at the top of each script:

Script Main settings 01 SEASON_START_MONTH (= 9, from regions.py), CROP_KEEP, IRRIGATED_TEXT, RAINFED_TEXT, CHECK_WORLDCOVER 02 REGION, N_FOLDS = 5, BLOCK_KM (= 20, from regions.py), CANDIDATE_KM, SEED = 42 03 REGION, TILE_PX = 128, GSD_M = 10, CRS_EPSG (= 32629, from regions.py), CHIP_PX = 64, MAX_SHIFT_PX = 8, INNER_BUFFER_M = 10, CLOUD_COVER_PERCENTAGE = 60, CS_THRESHOLD = 0.60, DOWNLOAD, SEASONS = None (all years; or one year at a time), DOWNLOAD_WORKERS = 8, N_TEST_TILES 04 REGION, SEASONS = None (all years → views/; one year → views_<year>/), CHIP_PATCH_SIZES = [8, 16], CHIP_PX = 64, S1_ORBIT = "auto", MAKE_FEATURES, MAKE_PIXELSETS

Earth Engine access uses a service-account key in secrets/, which is never committed.

docs.title: 11. Known limitations
docs.text:
• Class balance and geography: 14% of parcels are rainfed, and 94% of those are in Doukkala. A model can partly learn "region" rather than "irrigation". Per-zone results should be reported.
  • Reprojection: the few parcels in UTM 30N are resampled to 29N.
  • Monthly composites: in cloudy winter months some parcels have no clear Sentinel-2 view (NODATA). The counts show where.
  • Segmentation with view D: a tile can hold parcels of two folds (mixed_folds), and context tiles reach across fold borders. Tile-level models need their own tile split, or a loss mask restricted to the training fold.
  • Labels: a single survey visit per parcel. Overlapping parcels are set to ignore and listed, but labels are not otherwise checked against imagery.

docs.title: Phase 1 · Data preparation
docs.text: Phase 1 provides the data on which all later phases rely: labelled reference parcels, a spatial partition for validation, and a common store of Sentinel-1/2 imagery from which every model input is derived. The design ensures that differences between models are attributable to the models rather than to their input data.

docs.title: Components
docs.text: Component Content Status Page 1a · Morocco training data 8,781 labelled cropland parcels (7,585 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed); 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; 2,987 tiles of 128 × 128 px with 12 monthly composites × 19 bands; parcel features, pixel sets and patch-aligned chips ✅ complete Morocco training data 1b · Utah training data (second study area; temporal test) 12,015 WRLU crop fields in 550 sampled cells: WRLU 2024 training year (5,000 irrigated, 1,013 rainfed) and WRLU 2021 test year (4,987 irrigated, 1,015 rainfed); 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; tile plan of 5,436 tiles 🔄 labels, folds and tile plan done; download and views to run Utah training data 1c · Multi-year imagery, Morocco tile store for 2021–2025 for the annual maps of RQ3 📝 prepared in Phase 5 –

docs.title: Pipeline
docs.text:
Step Script Output 1 ml_dataset_prep/01_prepare_labels_Morocco.py or 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py cleaned, labelled cropland parcels (one script per region, same output layout) 2 ml_dataset_prep/02_make_spatial_folds.py fold (0–4) per parcel 3 ml_dataset_prep/03_build_tiles.py tile store from Google Earth Engine 4 ml_dataset_prep/04_make_views.py model inputs (views A–C) check models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py dataset inspection figures

Scripts 02–04 and the inspection serve both regions: set REGION = "morocco" or "utah" at the top. The settings that differ per region (projection, agricultural year, block size, map boundaries) are in ml_dataset_prep/regions.py. All outputs of a region are in outputs/<region>/ (dataset/, and for Morocco also study/ and analysis/).

The scripts, design choices, figures and output formats are documented in Morocco training data and Utah training data. The data providers are listed in Data sources; departures from the proposal are recorded as decisions D1, D2, D4 and D9.

docs.title: Reuse in later phases
docs.text: The scripts are region- and period-independent: the Utah dataset (1b) is produced with the same scripts 02–04, and the multi-year imagery (1c) by changing the agricultural years.

docs.title: Utah training data
docs.text:
This page describes the Utah dataset, the second, independent study area (D13). It is built with the same pipeline as the Morocco training data: only the label script (01_prepare_labels_Utah.py) is region-specific; scripts 02–04 are the same files, run with REGION = "utah".

Status

Labels (01), spatial folds (02) and the tile plan with label rasters (03, DOWNLOAD = False) are complete for WRLU 2024 (training year) and WRLU 2021 (temporal test year). The Sentinel-1/2 download (03) and the model views (04) have not been run yet; they run one year at a time, 2024 first.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
Step Script What comes out 1 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py 12,015 labelled crop fields in 550 sampled cells: WRLU 2024 (5,000 irrigated, 1,013 rainfed) and WRLU 2021 (4,987 irrigated, 1,015 rainfed); plus all 245,648 labelled crop fields of both years before sampling 2 02_make_spatial_folds.py (REGION = "utah") a fold (0–4) per field, from 183 spatial blocks of 20 km 3 03_build_tiles.py (REGION = "utah") tile plan: 5,436 tiles (2,720 for 2023/24, 2,716 for 2020/21); label rasters written 4 04_make_views.py (REGION = "utah") model inputs A–C as for Morocco, one folder per year (views_2023-24/, views_2020-21/)

All outputs are in outputs/utah/dataset/ (01_labels/, 02_folds/, 03_tiles_128px/agyear/), with the same file names and columns as outputs/morocco/dataset/.

docs.title: 2. Study design
docs.text:
• Utah is an independent second study area. There is no Morocco → Utah transfer: each region is trained and tested on its own data, with the same pipeline, foundation models, classifiers and evaluation, and the results are reported side by side. This tests whether the conclusions from Morocco hold in a second region with other crops, climate and labels.
  • Two questions in Utah:
    1. how well the models separate irrigated from rainfed fields (spatial cross-validation, as in Morocco);
    2. temporal transferability: whether a model trained on one year still works in another year (section 10).
  • Training year: WRLU 2024 (agricultural year 2023/24). Temporal test year: WRLU 2021 (2020/21).

docs.title: 3. Why Utah
docs.text:
The candidates were compared in D10 (Tunisia, eastern Washington, Utah, the IrrMap states):

  • An explicit rainfed class. The WRLU metadata defines IRR_Method = "Dry Crop" as a field with no irrigation, watered by natural processes (rain). IrrMap labels only the irrigation method (no rainfed class), and Colorado (CRDSS) and most layers of the USGS verified irrigated lands are irrigated-only.
  • Enough rainfed fields: 13,000–17,000 rainfed crop fields every year (figure below). Tunisia has 10 rainfed GMIA-NEXT points.
  • Every year from 2017 to 2025, mapped by one agency with one method, so the same pipeline also gives a temporal test.

WRLU crop fields (grain/seeds, hay/turf, field crops) per year and class, before sampling.

docs.title: 4. Source data
docs.text: Data Use Details Water-Related Land Use (WRLU), Utah Division of Water Resources labels one polygon layer per year, 2017–2025; all agricultural fields of Utah and of the parts of its river basins in Idaho, Wyoming, Colorado, Nevada and Arizona; crop (Descriptio, CropGroup), irrigation method (IRR_Method), basin, county, state. In data/Utah_field_data/ FAO GAUL 2024 (level 1) maps state outlines (data/admin_boundaries/) ESA WorldCover 2021 (10 m) label check optional: needs a raster covering Utah (ESA_WorldCover_10m_2021_Utah.tif); not yet available, so the check was skipped Sentinel-2 L2A, Cloud Score+, Sentinel-1 GRD imagery as for Morocco (Google Earth Engine)

docs.title: 5. Which years, and how the labels change between years
docs.text:
Agricultural year. WRLU year Y describes the crops of the growing season Y. The dataset uses the US water year, 1 October (Y−1) to 30 September (Y), written as for Morocco: WRLU 2024 → 2023/24, WRLU 2021 → 2020/21. It covers winter wheat from its autumn sowing to the July harvest, the whole irrigation season (mid-April to mid-October) and June–September, when irrigated and dry crops differ most. A calendar year would start in snow and cut off the autumn sowing. As in Morocco, every field gets the 12 monthly composites of its own year.

How much changes between years. All labelled crop fields of each year (the whole of WRLU, not only the sample) were compared with WRLU 2024. A field counts as the same field when its outline overlaps a 2024 outline with an intersection over union above 0.8 (outputs/utah/dataset/01_labels/year_change_vs_2024.csv):

WRLU year Labelled crop fields Same outline as in 2024 Crop changed Irrigation method changed Class changed (irrigated ↔ rainfed) 2024 122,624 (15,276 rainfed) – – – – 2025 123,722 121,811 (98.5%) 6.3% 17.4%¹ 28 (0.02%) 2023 121,029 116,492 (96.3%) 27.1% 0.1% 17 (0.01%) 2021 123,024 110,821 (90.1%) 35.7% 0.7% 83 (0.07%) 2019 121,063 100,491 (83.0%) 38.0% 2.7% 1,352 (1.35%) 2017 117,901 92,054 (78.1%) 40.6% 3.0% 1,307 (1.42%)

¹ Mostly a change of coding: in 2025 WRLU split Sprinkler into Sprinkler, Pivot and Wheel (wheel line).

  • Field outlines change slowly (78–98% unchanged).
  • Crops change a lot through rotation (27–41% after 1–7 years).
  • Irrigated vs rainfed hardly ever changes (0.01–0.07% since 2021). In Utah, irrigation depends on a water right and on canals, pivots and wells tied to the land; part of the stability may also come from labels carried over between map updates, which the data cannot separate.

Choice of years:

  • WRLU 2024 = training year: recent, actively updated (27% of the crops changed from 2023), and it overlaps the Moroccan survey years.
  • WRLU 2021 = temporal test year: three years earlier; 36% of the crops differ from 2024 while the labels stay consistent (83 class changes in 123,024 fields), so the test isolates the change of year (crops, weather, timing). 2021 was a drought year in Utah (drought emergency declared in March 2021), a realistic year-to-year shift that is reported as context. It still has both Sentinel-1 satellites (Sentinel-1B failed in December 2021).
  • Not 2025: 94% of its crops repeat 2024, so it looks largely carried over and is no independent test.
  • Not 2019 (for now): the jump from 83 class changes (2021) to 1,352 (2019) is sudden and may come from a revision of the mapping rather than from real change; it would need checking first.
  • Not all years: the labels are near-copies, so more years add volume but little information, at about 10 GB of tiles per year.

docs.title: 6. Script 01 — labels
docs.text:
1. Source inspection for every year in FILES: fields and area per crop group and irrigation method (source_counts.csv, source_years.png).
  2. Read the years in YEARS (agricultural fields only) and clean the geometry as for Morocco: repair invalid polygons, drop empty and duplicate geometries.

  3. Label:

    IRR_Method Label Flood, Sprinkler, Drip; from 2025 also Pivot and Wheel 1 · irrigated Dry Crop 2 · rainfed Sub-irrigated (natural high water table) dropped: neither class

  4. Crop fields only (CROP_GROUPS): grain/seeds, hay/turf and field crops. Fallow/idle land and pasture are dropped (no crop to observe, or grazing land rather than cropland). Garden, orchard and small fruit are dropped too: they are small groups, and orchards are almost all irrigated in Utah (19 "Dry Crop" orchards in 2023), so they would only add an easy irrigated class.

  5. All labelled crop fields before sampling (EXPORT_ALL_FIELDS = True): every labelled crop field of YEARS goes to all_crop_fields.gpkg (for QGIS) with a column sampled that marks the fields of the sampled cells, plus summary tables and figures, so the sample can be compared with the whole population:

    WRLU year Irrigated Rainfed In the sample 2024 107,348 15,276 5,000 irrigated (4.7%), 1,013 rainfed (6.6%) 2021 107,035 15,989 4,987 irrigated (4.7%), 1,015 rainfed (6.3%)

  6. Attributes with the Morocco names: parcel_id (UT<year>_<feature id>), ag_season, label, class_name, crop, zone (= river basin), area_ha, nn_dist_m (nearest field of the same year). Utah extras: year, state, county, crop_group, irr_method, cell_id. WRLU has no survey date, so date is empty.

How many fields are dropped on the way (WRLU 2024): 283,781 polygons in the file → 190,269 agricultural (urban, water, wetland and other land removed) → 122,624 labelled crop fields (fallow, pasture, sub-irrigated, orchard, garden and small fruit removed) → 6,013 in the sampled cells.

All labelled crop fields of WRLU 2024 and 2021 before sampling.

Main crops per class, all labelled crop fields of both years. Alfalfa is the main crop of both classes.

docs.title: 7. Script 01 — sampling of cells
docs.text:
Why a sample and not all fields. All labelled crop fields would be about 122,000 fields per year: roughly 20,000 tiles (~75 GB) and ~170 GB of model views per year, and 15–20 times the embedding time of Morocco, for little extra independent information. The statistics are limited by the rainfed class and by the number of spatial blocks, not by the number of fields: fields in the same block are strongly alike (89% of field pairs closer than 1 km share their class), and the block bootstrap counts blocks. The sample also keeps the Utah dataset close to the size of the Moroccan one (8,781 parcels), so model differences are not a matter of data volume.

Three nested units:

Unit Size Role Field median 2.5 ha one sample with its label Cell 1.28 × 1.28 km = one 128-px tile of script 03 the sampling unit: a cell is sampled with all its fields, or not at all Block 20 × 20 km (~240 cells) the fold unit of script 02; also used to spread the sample

Both grids start at the origin of UTM 12N: cell = (⌊x / 1,280 m⌋, ⌊y / 1,280 m⌋), block = (⌊x / 20,000 m⌋, ⌊y / 20,000 m⌋). A field belongs to the cell and to the block that contain its centroid.

Algorithm (sample_cells: stratified random sampling with a cap per block):

  1. Cells with at least one labelled crop field in any of YEARS (both years pooled): 12,424 cells.
  2. Two strata: "with rainfed" = at least one rainfed field in either year; "irrigated only" = the rest.
  3. Random order within each stratum (fixed seed SEED = 42, so every run gives the same cells).
  4. Cap: going down the shuffled list, a cell is skipped once its 20 km block already has MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK (6) cells of that stratum. Without the cap the densest valleys (Cache Valley, Bear River) would take most of the sample.
  5. The first N_RAINFED_CELLS (400) and N_IRRIGATED_CELLS (150) cells are kept: 550 cells in 176 blocks.
  6. The same cells are used for every year in YEARS; every labelled crop field inside a sampled cell is kept.

What is labelled inside a sampled tile:

In the tile Label raster crop fields (grain, hay, field crops), irrigated or Dry Crop, whose centroid lies in the cell 1 irrigated / 2 rainfed fallow, pasture, orchards, sub-irrigated fields 0 = ignore roads, towns, natural land 0 = ignore a field centred in a neighbouring, not sampled cell that reaches into the tile 0 = ignore

A labelled field is always complete: when its outline crosses into the next tile, that tile is built as well ("outline" tile). Within a 20 km block at most 12 cells (6 + 6) are sampled, i.e. at most ~5% of its area is labelled. Labels are therefore dense within a sampled cell and sparse within a block, as in Morocco, where the survey did not label every field either.

Result:

Agricultural year Irrigated Rainfed Rainfed share 2020/21 (WRLU 2021, test year) 4,987 1,015 16.9% 2023/24 (WRLU 2024, training year) 5,000 1,013 16.8% Total 9,987 2,028 16.9%

Rainfed fields are over-represented on purpose (16.9% of the sample against 12.5–13% of all fields), which makes the rainfed F1 more reliable. Median field size is 2.5 ha in both classes, three times the Moroccan median (0.83 ha). By state: 8,234 + 1,057 fields in Utah, 1,707 + 849 in Idaho (Bear River basin), the rest in Colorado and Wyoming (irrigated + rainfed). 1,171 of the 2,028 rainfed fields (58%) are in the Bear River basin.

Cells of 1.28 km with crop fields in WRLU 2024 or 2021 (grey) and the sampled cells: with a rainfed field in either year (red), irrigated only (blue). The same cells are used for both years.

Sampled reference fields, WRLU 2024 and 2021.

Main crops per class in the sample. Rainfed fields are mostly dryland alfalfa, winter wheat and grass hay.

Larger samples are a change of N_RAINFED_CELLS / N_IRRIGATED_CELLS and a re-run of 01–03:

Option Cells Fields per year (approx.) Cost relative to now now 400 + 150 ~6,000 1× double 800 + 300 ~12,000 ~2× all cells with rainfed + matching irrigated-only ~4,800 + 1,500 ~60,000 ~10× all fields (SAMPLE = False) ~12,400 ~122,000 ~20×

Outputs (outputs/utah/dataset/01_labels/): parcels_labelled.geojson (the sample), source_counts.csv, summary.csv, summary_by_zone.csv, sampled_cells.csv, year_change_vs_2024.csv; before sampling: all_crop_fields.gpkg, all_fields_summary.csv, all_fields_by_zone.csv, all_fields_*.png; figures.

docs.title: 8. Script 02 — spatial folds
docs.text:
The same script as for Morocco (REGION = "utah"). The class-similarity curve uses only pairs of fields of the same agricultural year: the same field in two years is not two independent samples.

Distance between fields ≤ 0.25 km 1 km 3 km 10 km 15 km 20 km random placement Pairs with the same class 92.1% 89.2% 80.2% 80.2% 70.5% 70.7% 71.9%

Class similarity reaches the random-placement level at about 15 km, so the 20 km block of Morocco is kept.

Split (average over the 5 rounds) Rainfed in smallest fold Test with train ≤ 250 m Test with train ≤ 1 km random 405 94.3% 99.4% blocks 5 km 405 6.5% 27.7% blocks 20 km 405 2.2% 9.8% blocks 50 km 336 0.3% 2.1%

Folds: 183 blocks, about 2,000 irrigated and 405 rainfed fields per fold. A field belongs to the block of its centroid, so the same place falls in the same block, and therefore in the same fold, in every year: a model is never trained on a place it is tested on, in either year. The greedy assignment places the blocks with the most rainfed fields first; the many small blocks with few fields come last, so one fold (here fold 0, 59 blocks) collects more, smaller blocks than the others (30–33). Morocco shows the same pattern (fold 2: 42 of 91 blocks).

Fields coloured by fold (left) and class counts per fold (right).

The 20 km blocks coloured by fold, with enlargements of the two densest areas: A on the Utah–Idaho border (Cache Valley, Bear River), B in central Utah. Whole blocks go to one fold.

docs.title: 9. Script 03 — tile store
docs.text:
The same script as for Morocco (REGION = "utah"). Grid, bands, cloud mask and file formats are unchanged (Morocco, section 6). Two settings come from regions.py: the projection (UTM 12N, EPSG:32612) and the first month (October, so m01 = October).

One tile per place and year. The tile name starts with the agricultural year, so the same place gets one tile per year, on the same pixel grid:

Training year (WRLU 2024) Test year (WRLU 2021) tile 2023-24_184_3383 2020-21_184_3383 image _img.tif Sentinel-1/2, Oct 2023 – Sep 2024 Sentinel-1/2, Oct 2020 – Sep 2021 label _lab.tif the 2024 fields and labels the 2021 fields and labels field in parcels.csv own parcel_id / parcel_idx own parcel_id / parcel_idx fold e.g. fold 3 the same fold 3

parcels.csv holds both years (6,013 fields of 2023/24 and 6,002 of 2020/21); their numbers never change when another year is downloaded.

Tile plan (DOWNLOAD = False): 12,015 fields; 6 smaller than one pixel centre; 280 with no pixel left after the 10 m inner buffer; no overlapping fields. 5,436 tiles (2,720 for 2023/24, 2,716 for 2020/21; 1,042 home tiles), about 10 GB of images per year. 120 tiles hold fields of two folds: a 20 km block is 15.6 cells wide, so some cells straddle a block border (the parcel models are not affected; segmentation needs the loss mask, as in Morocco).

docs.title: 10. Temporal test design
docs.text:
Because the training year and the test year use the same cells, the test fold holds the same fields in both years. Per round of the 5-fold rotation:

Score Train Test Measures A · same year 2024, training folds 2024, test fold spatial accuracy, as in Morocco B · new year, new places 2024, training folds 2021, test fold temporal transferability (main result) C · new year, seen places 2024, training folds 2021, training-fold fields change of imagery only (upper bound: places seen in training)
  • B − A is the cost of the change of year, measured on identical fields (a paired comparison, so the block bootstrap gives a narrow interval).
  • Within B, the fields whose crop changed between the two years show where a new year matters most.
  • The test asks whether a model recognises irrigation in a different year with other crops and weather. It cannot test the detection of changes in irrigation (83 class changes in the whole of WRLU).
  • The training script needs a "train on one year, test on another" option; it is added before the 2021 test.

docs.title: 11. Differences from Morocco
docs.text: Morocco Utah Labels field survey, Dec 2023 – Jan 2025 agency land-use map (WRLU), mostly image interpretation; 1,987 fields field-checked in 2025 Rainfed definition "rainfed" in the survey IRR_Method = "Dry Crop" Crops seasonal crops and trees grain, hay and field crops (no orchards) Selection all surveyed parcels 550 sampled 1.28 km cells, all fields inside Years 2023/24 and 2024/25, pooled 2023/24 (training) and 2020/21 (temporal test), kept apart Agricultural year 1 Sep – 31 Aug 1 Oct – 30 Sep (water year) Projection UTM 29N UTM 12N zone irrigation district river basin Median field size 0.83 ha 2.5 ha Rainfed share 13.6% 16.9%

docs.title: 12. Running, one year at a time
docs.text:
conda activate condaml
python ml_dataset_prep/01_prepare_labels_Utah.py     # ~1 min; YEARS = [2024, 2021]
# in 02, 03 and 04 set REGION = "utah" at the top, then:
python ml_dataset_prep/02_make_spatial_folds.py      # seconds
python ml_dataset_prep/03_build_tiles.py             # SEASONS = ["2023/24"]; first N_TEST_TILES = 20; Earth Engine, resumable
python ml_dataset_prep/04_make_views.py              # SEASONS = ["2023/24"] -> views_2023-24/
python models_run/01_inspect_dataset.py              # REGION = "utah", VIEWS_NAME = "views_2023-24"

Run everything in the condaml environment: another GDAL / GEOS version once gave one field more.

Step Runs for Why 01 labels, 02 folds all years in YEARS at once (local, ~1 min) sampled cells, parcel numbers and folds are fixed once, the same for every year 03 plan + label rasters all years (local, seconds) the parcel numbers in the label rasters never change 03 Earth Engine download only the years in SEASONS 2024 first (["2023/24"]), 2021 later (["2020/21"]); finished tiles are skipped 04 views only the years in SEASONS each year in its own folder: views_2023-24/, views_2020-21/

Running 01 with one year only and adding the other year later would redraw the cells and rebalance the folds, and the two years would no longer be paired.

Region settings (ml_dataset_prep/regions.py): crs_epsg = 32612, start_month = 10, block_km = 20, map boundaries. Utah settings in 01_prepare_labels_Utah.py: YEARS, CROP_GROUPS, EXCLUDE_CROPS, IRRIGATED_METHODS, RAINFED_METHODS, STATES, EXPORT_ALL_FIELDS, SAMPLE, CELL_M, N_RAINFED_CELLS, N_IRRIGATED_CELLS, MAX_CELLS_PER_BLOCK, SEED.

docs.title: 13. Known limitations
docs.text:
• Labels are not a field survey. WRLU is mapped mainly from imagery with field checks on part of the area, and lists the Cropland Data Layer among its inputs. Its errors are not known per field.
  • Labels barely change between years (section 5): the temporal test measures robustness to a new year, not change detection, and it must hold out space (score B).
  • Unequal inclusion probabilities. Rainfed areas are favoured, and cells in crowded blocks are less likely to be sampled. This is fine for comparing models (all see the same fields), but the scores are not unbiased accuracy estimates for all Utah fields; that would need sampling weights. The same holds for Morocco, whose survey is not a probability sample either.
  • Dryland alfalfa is the largest rainfed crop (1,122 of 2,028). It is perennial and green in spring, unlike the Moroccan rainfed cereals. EXCLUDE_CROPS = ["Alfalfa"] gives a sensitivity run.
  • Class and place: 58% of the rainfed fields lie in the Bear River basin (northern Utah and south-east Idaho), so results are also reported per basin, as per zone in Morocco.
  • Snow: December–February composites in northern Utah often show snow (Cloud Score+ does not mask snow); both classes are affected alike.
  • Sentinel-1: 2021 has both Sentinel-1 satellites, 2024 only Sentinel-1A, so about twice as many Sentinel-1 scenes per month in the test year.
  • WorldCover check not yet run (no Utah raster).

docs.title: Evaluation protocol
docs.text:
This protocol defines the rules common to all experiments and ensures that results are comparable across inputs, classifiers and experiments. Any deviation must be declared in the experiment's What changes table.

Contents: 1 Task · 2 Splits · 3 Inputs · 4 Classifiers · 5 Temporal aggregation · 6 Fairness rules · 7 Metrics · 8 Reading a result · 9 Reporting · References

docs.title: 1. Task and unit
docs.text: The task is binary classification of parcels into irrigated (class 1) and rainfed (class 2), with one label and one prediction per surveyed parcel; all metrics are computed at parcel level. 8,781 parcels (7,585 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed); inputs are scored on the parcels present in every run (8,775: six parcels fully covered by overlapping polygons have no own pixel).

docs.title: 2. Spatial splits
docs.text:
Parcels are grouped into 20 km blocks, and the blocks into 5 folds with the same class balance (about 1,530 irrigated and 240 rainfed parcels each). A block is never split. A place surveyed in both seasons stays in one fold. Block size and fold assignment: dataset §5.

Main design: PASTIS rotation (Garnot & Landrieu 2021). Five rounds; in each, 3 folds train, the next fold is the validation fold, one fold is the test fold:

Round Train Validation (choose settings / early stopping) Test 1 2, 3, 4 1 0 2 3, 4, 0 2 1 3 4, 0, 1 3 2 4 0, 1, 2 4 3 5 1, 2, 3 0 4

The model is trained on the 3 training folds with the setting that scored best on the validation fold. The test fold is never used for any choice. After 5 rounds every parcel has one out-of-fold prediction from a model that never saw its block. Classifiers and neural networks use the same rotation.

Why a rotation rather than one fixed split. (i) Every parcel is tested once, so the rainfed scores rest on all 1,196 rainfed parcels instead of the ~240 of a single test fold. (ii) Five different test areas reveal how strongly accuracy depends on the region, which a single test area would show only by chance. (iii) Hyperparameters are never chosen on the test fold, so the reported accuracy is not inflated by tuning (Varma & Simon, 2006). The same principle of spatially separated folds is implemented in blockCV (Valavi et al., 2019) and used for crop-type classification with Sentinel-1/2 by Orynbaikyzy et al. (2022); Schratz et al. (2019) recommend spatial folds for tuning as well as for testing.

Sensitivity design: nested spatial CV (VALIDATION: nested, experiment E01): settings chosen by spatial CV on the 4 non-test folds, model refit on all 4.

Random CV (stratified, ignoring blocks) is only used inside a run to show how much it overstates accuracy.

docs.title: 3. Inputs
docs.text: Five inputs are compared, all Sentinel-2 only (D14): a Sentinel-2 parcel-feature baseline (12 Sentinel-2 bands, NDVI, NDWI, EVI over 12 months; 180 features) and the embeddings of four frozen foundation models (Clay v1.5, Prithvi-EO-2.0, TerraMind, AgriFM). A parcel's embedding is the mean of the patch embeddings that cover it, weighted by the share of each patch inside the parcel; chips are 64 × 64 px and shifted so that the parcel centroid lies at a patch centre. Bands, patch size and temporal handling per model: Foundation models · Configuration.

docs.title: 4. Classifiers
docs.text:
Classifier Grid (chosen on the validation fold, by macro-F1) Fixed logreg logistic regression (linear probe) C ∈ balanced classes, standardised rf random forest max_features ∈ {√p, 0.3} · min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 5} · class_weight ∈ {none, balanced_subsample} 500 trees svm RBF support vector machine C ∈ {1, 10} · γ ∈ {scale, 0.01} balanced classes, standardised

Headline classifiers: random forest (the proposal's baseline classifier) for every input, and logistic regression (linear probe) for the foundation models. SVM is always reported. Histogram gradient boosting was used in E01 and is dropped from E02 on (D6). A trainable MLP head is added in E03 and E04 (experiment plan).

docs.title: 5. Temporal aggregation: two pipelines
docs.text:
How the 12 monthly embeddings of a parcel become one input for the classifier is the step that differs between the two pipelines. Everything before (embeddings) and after (comparison, metrics) is shared.

flowchart LR E["<b>Monthly embeddings</b><br/>12 × D per parcel<br/>(AgriFM: 1 × D)"] --> A["<b>PCA pipeline</b><br/>fill empty months (training median)<br/>→ concat 12 months → standardise<br/>→ PCA 128, fitted on the training folds"] E --> B["<b>L-TAE pipeline</b><br/>standardise per channel<br/>→ L-TAE attention over the months<br/>(empty months masked)"] A --> C["LogReg · RF · SVM (E02)<br/>or MLP (E03)"] B --> D["MLP head, trained with the L-TAE<br/>early stopping on the validation fold<br/>3 seeds"] C --> O["<b>oof_predictions.csv</b><br/>same format"] D --> O O --> CMP["compare: same parcels,<br/>same bootstrap draws"] PCA pipeline L-TAE pipeline Experiments E01, E02, E03 E04 Learns which months matter no (PCA is unsupervised) yes (attention weights) Keeps the order of the months only as positions in the vector yes (positional encoding) Classifier the three of §4 (E02) or an MLP (E03) its own MLP head Applies to the baseline yes (180 features, no PCA) yes (15 variables × 12 months) Applies to AgriFM yes no (one vector per year) Reference linear probing of frozen features PANGAEA: single-date encoders + L-TAE (Marsocci et al. 2024); L-TAE (Garnot & Landrieu 2020)

The L-TAE pipeline is also trained on the monthly Sentinel-2 features, so that the baseline benefits from the same temporal model and the comparison remains balanced. Because both pipelines write the same out-of-fold predictions, E04 compares them directly with the E02 runs on the same parcels.

docs.title: 6. Fairness rules
docs.text:
flowchart LR subgraph SAME["Identical for every input"] P1["same parcels<br/>(common to all runs)"] P2["same pixels<br/>(one tile store)"] P3["same folds<br/>and rotation"] P4["same classifiers<br/>and grids"] P5["same metrics and<br/>bootstrap draws"] end SAME --> D["only the input<br/>(or the one setting the<br/>experiment varies) differs"] D --> C["paired difference<br/>with 95% CI"]
  1. Every fitted step (imputation, standardisation, PCA, tuning, early stopping) uses the training folds only; the validation fold only chooses settings; the test fold is used once, for the prediction.
  2. All inputs come from the same tile store: same composites, cloud mask, months and parcels.
  3. Settings are chosen with the same budget for every input (the grids above).
  4. Inputs are compared on the parcels common to all runs, with the same bootstrap draws.
  5. An experiment varies one thing against the experiment it builds on, and says so in its README.

docs.title: 7. Metrics and uncertainty
docs.text:
Metric Role Macro-F1 headline: mean of irrigated F1 and rainfed F1, so the 14% rainfed class counts equally F1, precision, recall per class rainfed recall: how many rainfed fields are found Balanced accuracy mean recall of both classes Overall accuracy for comparison with the literature (predicting "all irrigated" already gives 86%) PR-AUC (rainfed), Brier score, ECE ranking quality and calibration of the predicted probabilities Macro-F1 per fold, mean ± SD stability across regions (the proposal's selection criterion)

The kappa coefficient is not reported, as it is uninformative for accuracy assessment (Pontius & Millones, 2011).

95% confidence intervals: block bootstrap (Künsch, 1989). The 91 blocks, not the parcels, are the independent units. Each of 1,000 draws resamples whole blocks with replacement and recomputes the metric; the 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles give the interval. The same 1,000 draws are used for every run, so a difference between two inputs is measured on identical resamples (paired).

docs.title: 8. How a result is read
docs.text:
• Δ macro-F1 = input − baseline, with the same classifier (runs with their own model, such as L-TAE or PSE-TAE, against the baseline random forest).
  • An input is better (or worse) than the baseline only if the 95% CI of Δ excludes 0 and the Holm-adjusted p-value is below 0.05. Holm corrects for testing all inputs × classifiers together.
  • A CI that excludes 0 without surviving Holm is reported as "higher / lower, not significant after Holm".
  • Otherwise: no clear difference. With ~240 rainfed parcels per fold, differences below about 0.02 macro-F1 are usually inside the noise.

docs.title: 9. Reporting standard
docs.text: Every experiment has a report page (docs/experiments/<name>/report.md) with, in this order: the answer in one or two sentences, the key findings, the setup, the result tables and figures (generated by experiments/make_report.py from the results), the interpretation, the caveats and the next steps. A finished experiment adds a one-line answer to its config.yaml, which appears on the Results page.

docs.title: RQ1 · Experiment plan
docs.text:
This page is the complete plan of the frozen-encoder evaluation of Phase 2 · Model evaluation (RQ1): which experiments are run, what each one answers, and every setting. It is agreed before the runs start; an experiment page in Experiments is created from it when the experiment is implemented. Rules shared by all experiments (splits, metrics, fairness) are in the evaluation protocol.

Contents: 1 Decisions · 2 Shared settings · 3 Inputs · 4 Design · 5 Main experiments · 6 Label efficiency · 7 Ablations · 8 Analyses · 9 Results pages · 10 Order of work · 11 Size · 12 Open points

Experiment pages (setup, settings, how to run; the report is added when the results are in):

ID Experiment Answers Page E02 PCA + LogReg / RF / SVM Q1 (main table of RQ1) E02 setup E03 PCA + MLP head Q2 · does the head matter? E03 setup E04 L-TAE + MLP head Q3 · does attention over the months help? E04 setup E05 PSE-TAE from scratch Q4 · is a model trained from scratch enough? E05 setup E01 PCA + classifiers, nested CV (done, before D14) check of the validation design E01 setup · report

Label efficiency (Q5) is part of every experiment E02–E05: each one also trains on 10, 25 and 50% of the training blocks (§6). All experiments: Experiments overview.

docs.title: 1. Decisions this plan rests on
docs.text: Decision Choice Reason Input data Sentinel-2 only for every foundation model and every baseline same optical data for all; Morocco and Utah treated alike; Sentinel-1 coverage of Utah changed between years (D14). Sentinel-1 is an ablation for later (A5). Model inputs each foundation model receives only the bands it was pretrained on; no fusion designed by us the comparison tests the pretrained models, not a fusion scheme Classifier heads three classical classifiers (logistic regression, random forest, SVM) and one neural head (MLP) linear probe = standard test of frozen features; RF = standard remote-sensing classifier; SVM = strongest in E01; MLP = trainable head as in GeoFM benchmarks. Gradient boosting is dropped: in E01 it was never the best and always within the CI of SVM (D6). Temporal handling PCA (concatenated months) and L-TAE (learned attention over the months) D8; L-TAE as in PANGAEA (Marsocci et al. 2024) Neural baseline from scratch PSE-TAE on the parcel pixel sets built for parcel classification from satellite time series (Garnot et al. 2020) Most important extra label efficiency the main claim for foundation models is that they need fewer labels Regions Morocco and Utah 2023/24, same protocol, analysed separately D13: two independent study areas

docs.title: 2. Settings shared by every experiment
docs.text: Setting Value Task irrigated (1) vs rainfed (2), one prediction per parcel Morocco data views views/ (2023/24 + 2024/25 pooled), 8,775 parcels scored (7,579 irrigated, 1,196 rainfed) Utah data views views_2023-24/ (WRLU 2024 labels), 6,011 parcels with pixels Time 12 monthly composites of the agricultural year (Morocco Sep–Aug, Utah Oct–Sep) Splits 5 spatial folds of 20 km blocks; PASTIS rotation: per round 3 folds train, the next fold validates (settings, early stopping), 1 fold tests Tuning grids below, chosen on the validation fold by macro-F1; same grid for every input Fitted steps imputation, standardisation, PCA, tuning and early stopping use the training folds only Neural networks 3 seeds (42, 1042, 2042) per run; mean ± SD over seeds; the out-of-fold prediction of a parcel is the mean probability of the 3 seeds Metrics macro-F1 (headline), F1 / precision / recall per class, balanced and overall accuracy, PR-AUC (rainfed), Brier, ECE Uncertainty block bootstrap, 1,000 draws, same draws for every run; paired differences; Holm over all comparisons of an experiment Comparison set parcels present in every run of the region

docs.title: 3. Inputs
docs.text:
All five inputs are cut from the same tile store. Sentinel-2 only.

Input Data per parcel Bands Patch Per parcel Months Script S2 baseline median of the parcel's inner pixels 12 S2 bands + NDVI, NDWI, EVI (15 variables) parcel 15 × 12 = 180 features 12 03 (view A) Clay v1.5 64 px chip, p8 grid 10 S2 bands 8 px (80 m) 12 × 1,024 12 02a Prithvi-EO-2.0 64 px chip, p16 grid 6 S2 bands (HLS set) 16 px (160 m) 12 × 1,024 12 02b TerraMind 64 px chip, p16 grid 12 S2 bands 16 px (160 m) 12 × 768 12 02c AgriFM 64 px chip, p16 grid 10 S2 bands 4 px patch, stride 32 px (320 m) 1 × 1,024 (whole year) 1 02d Pixel sets (PSE-TAE only) all inner pixels of the parcel 10 S2 bands pixel N pixels × 12 × 10 12 03b (view B)

Patch embeddings are pooled over the parcel with the patch-share weights (models pipeline §5). Clay and Prithvi also receive the parcel location and the date, as in their pretraining; A4 tests whether the location acts as a shortcut.

docs.title: 4. Design: what is varied
docs.text:
Three things are varied: the input, the temporal handling and the head. Not every combination exists: L-TAE is a neural network trained with its own loss, so it cannot feed a random forest, and AgriFM gives one vector per year, so it has no months for L-TAE.

flowchart LR IN["<b>Input</b><br/>S2 baseline · Clay · Prithvi<br/>TerraMind · AgriFM"] --> PCA["<b>PCA</b><br/>12 months concatenated<br/>→ PCA 128"] IN --> LT["<b>L-TAE</b><br/>attention over<br/>the 12 months"] PCA --> CL["<b>Classical</b><br/>LogReg · RF · SVM"] PCA --> MLP1["<b>MLP</b>"] LT --> MLP2["<b>MLP</b><br/>(trained with L-TAE)"] PX["<b>Pixel sets</b><br/>S2, from scratch"] --> PS["<b>PSE-TAE</b>"] CL --> E02(["E02"]) MLP1 --> E03(["E03"]) MLP2 --> E04(["E04"]) PS --> E05(["E05"]) Cell Temporal handling Head S2 baseline Clay Prithvi TerraMind AgriFM Experiment a PCA LogReg · RF · SVM ✓ (no PCA) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ E02 b PCA MLP ✓ (no PCA) ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ E03 c L-TAE MLP ✓ ✓ ✓ ✓ – E04 d from scratch PSE-TAE pixel sets – – – – E05

Which comparison answers which question

Question Comparison Same in both Q1 · Do frozen foundation-model embeddings beat Sentinel-2 features? each GeoFM vs the S2 baseline, within E02, E03 and E04 head, temporal handling, parcels Q2 · Does the head matter? E02 vs E03 (classical vs MLP) input, PCA Q3 · Does learning which months matter help? E03 vs E04 (PCA vs L-TAE) input, MLP head Q4 · Is a model trained from scratch on our labels enough? E05 vs the best GeoFM setting and the best baseline setting parcels, folds Q5 · Do foundation models need fewer labels? learning curves inside E02–E05 (10 / 25 / 50 / 100% of the training blocks) everything except the training size Q6 · Do the conclusions hold in a second region? every question in Morocco and in Utah protocol

The S2 baseline in E04 (L-TAE on the 15 monthly variables) is the key control for Q1: if L-TAE helps the GeoFMs, the same L-TAE must be given to the raw features, otherwise the gain could come from L-TAE rather than from the embeddings.

docs.title: E02 · PCA + classical classifiers
docs.text:
Setup page: E02

Question Q1 with the classical heads; the main table of RQ1 Inputs S2 baseline, Clay, Prithvi, TerraMind, AgriFM Temporal handling months with no clear pixel filled with the training-fold median → 12 months concatenated → standardised → PCA 128 (fitted on the training folds). AgriFM: 1 × 1,024 → PCA 128. Baseline: 180 features, gaps filled by linear interpolation in time per parcel, standardised, no PCA. Classifiers and grids logreg C ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10}, balanced classes · rf 500 trees, max_features ∈ {√p, 0.3}, min_samples_leaf ∈ {1, 5}, class_weight ∈ {none, balanced_subsample} · svm RBF, C ∈ {1, 10}, γ ∈ {scale, 0.01}, balanced classes Headline logistic regression (linear probe) for the GeoFMs; random forest for the baseline, as in the protocol; all three reported Runs 5 inputs × 2 regions = 10 runs (3 classifiers each) Script models_run/03_train_evaluate.py

docs.title: E03 · PCA + MLP
docs.text:
Setup page: E03

Question Q2: does a trainable neural head get more out of the same PCA input than the classical heads? Inputs the same 128 PCA components (baseline: the 180 standardised features) as E02 Head MLP 128 → 256 → 128 → 2, ReLU, batch normalisation, dropout 0.2 (same hidden sizes as the E04 head) Training AdamW, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, class-weighted cross-entropy, up to 100 epochs, early stopping on validation macro-F1 (patience 15), 3 seeds Tuning none beyond early stopping (same budget for every input) Runs 5 inputs × 2 regions × 3 seeds Script models_run/03c_train_ltae.py, HEAD: mlp on the PCA input

docs.title: E04 · L-TAE + MLP
docs.text:
Setup page: E04

Question Q3: does attention over the months classify better than concatenation + PCA? Inputs monthly sequences: S2 baseline (12 × 15 variables), Clay (12 × 1,024), Prithvi (12 × 1,024), TerraMind (12 × 768). AgriFM excluded (one vector per year). Pre-processing per-channel standardisation with training-fold statistics; months without a clear pixel are masked in the attention, not filled Model L-TAE (Garnot & Landrieu 2020) with the paper's default size: 16 heads, d_k 8, d_model 256, output MLP 256-128; then a linear layer with 2 outputs; sinusoidal encoding of each month's mid-month day (days since the start of the agricultural year), as in L-TAE Training as E03 (AdamW 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, class-weighted cross-entropy, ≤ 100 epochs, patience 15, 3 seeds) Runs 4 inputs × 2 regions × 3 seeds Script models_run/03c_train_ltae.py, HEAD: ltae Compared with the E03 run of the same input (same head, PCA instead of L-TAE) and the E02 runs

docs.title: E05 · PSE-TAE from scratch
docs.text:
Setup page: E05

Question Q4: does a temporal deep model trained only on our labelled parcels match the frozen foundation models? Input pixel sets: inner pixels of the parcel (edge pixels within 10 m left out; parcels with < 4 inner pixels keep all), 10 S2 bands × 12 months Model PSE-TAE (Garnot et al. 2020): 64 pixels sampled per parcel and month; at prediction the mean of 5 random pixel draws Training Adam 1e-3, weight decay 1e-4, batch 128, ≤ 100 epochs, early stopping on validation macro-F1 (patience 15), 3 seeds Runs morocco_s2, utah_s2 × 3 seeds Script models_run/03b_train_psetae.py (N_SEEDS = 3)

docs.title: 6. Label efficiency (inside E02–E05)
docs.text:
Label efficiency is not a separate experiment: every experiment E02–E05 also trains each input on fewer training blocks, and its report shows the learning curve next to the main result. The block draws are shared, so the curves of all experiments are directly comparable.

Question Q5: how much training data does each input and head need? Foundation models are expected to gain most when labels are few; the heads with many trained parameters (MLP, L-TAE, PSE-TAE) may lose most. Training size 10, 25 and 50% of the training blocks of each round; 100% = the main run. Validation and test folds stay complete, so only the amount of training data changes. Sampling whole blocks: rainfed and irrigated-only blocks each put in a random order (per region, round and draw), and a fraction takes the first blocks of each list, so the draws are nested (10% ⊂ 25% ⊂ 50%); the order is accepted only if its first 10% hold ≥ 20 rainfed parcels. No fraction below 10%. (In Morocco most rainfed parcels lie in a few Doukkala blocks.) Repeats 3 draws per fraction; draw k is the same in every experiment, for every input and head (paired) Seeds neural runs (E03–E05): 1 seed per draw (the draws give the spread); the main runs keep 3 seeds, and their 100% point on the curve is scored seed by seed, so every point is single-seed Settings label_efficiency block in each experiment's config.yaml; TRAIN_FRACTION and FRACTION_DRAW in scripts 03, 03b and 03c (one shared block-drawing function) Runs per region: E02 45, E03 45, E04 36, E05 9 = 135; 270 for both regions Result in each report: macro-F1 and rainfed F1 vs training fraction, one line per input; in the RQ1 synthesis: all experiments together, the fraction at which each GeoFM reaches the full-data score of the baseline, and whether the best head or PCA vs L-TAE changes with fewer labels Caveat tuning and early stopping still use the complete validation fold, slightly optimistic for a real low-label situation

docs.title: 7. Ablations
docs.text:
Short, targeted runs; each changes one setting of a main experiment.

ID Question Change On Priority A1 Does the yearly profile matter at all? average of the 12 monthly embeddings instead of concat + PCA (FEATURE_MODE: mean) E02, linear probe + SVM high (cheap) A2 Is the PCA size a fragile choice? PCA 32 / 64 / 128 / 256 E02, linear probe medium A3 How many months are needed? 1 peak month / 4 seasonal months / 12 months best setting of each input optional A4 Do Clay and Prithvi use the location as a shortcut? location input switched off (Prithvi USE_COORDS = False, Clay location set to zero); re-embedding needed E02, Morocco (rainfed parcels concentrated in Doukkala) high A5 Does Sentinel-1 add information? TerraMind with Sentinel-1 (terramind-s1s2), baseline with radar features (S1S2_VARIABLES: all), PSE-TAE morocco_s2s1 E02, E04, E05, Morocco only later

E01 (nested spatial CV, done before D14 with Sentinel-1 in the baseline and in TerraMind) stays as the check of the validation design.

docs.title: 8. Analyses on every run
docs.text:
From the out-of-fold predictions; no new training.

Analysis Why Script Paired differences vs the baseline, Holm-adjusted main test of Q1 04_compare_models.py Results by zone, season, parcel size and patch purity region shortcut (Morocco rainfed in Doukkala); small parcels inside 160 m patches 05_breakdown_oof.py Results by crop group (Utah: rainfed alfalfa vs grain) where each input fails later: 05_breakdown_oof.py extension (needs the crop names joined from 01_labels) Random vs spatial CV how much random CV overstates accuracy 03_train_evaluate.py Calibration (Brier, ECE) usable probabilities for maps 03, 03b, 03c Month importance (permutation, L-TAE attention) which part of the season separates the classes 03, 03c Compute cost: parameters, embedding time, training time practical value collected by hand from the run logs

docs.title: 9. Results pages
docs.text:
Every experiment gets its own pages in Experiments, created when it is implemented and filled after each run:

  • index.md (setup): question, what changes against the previous experiment, all settings, how to run.
  • report.md (results): the answer in one or two sentences first, then the generated tables and figures, then the interpretation, caveats and next steps (protocol §9).

Tables and figures are written by experiments/make_report.py from the results, so a page always matches its run. With two regions, every table and figure appears once for Morocco and once for Utah.

Experiment Tables Figures every experiment metrics with 95% CI per input × head; macro-F1 per training fraction (label efficiency); differences vs the baseline (Δ macro-F1, CI, Holm) ; per-fold macro-F1 macro-F1 with CI per input; learning curve (10–100% of the training blocks); macro-F1 per test fold; confusion matrices E02 · PCA + classical the three classifiers side by side; results by zone (focus zone, irrigated-only zones) month importance (permutation, random forest) per input; breakdown by zone and parcel area E03 · PCA + MLP MLP vs the E02 classifiers on the same input; macro-F1 per seed training curves (validation macro-F1 per epoch) E04 · L-TAE + MLP L-TAE vs PCA (E03) on the same input; macro-F1 per seed attention weight per month and class; training curves E05 · PSE-TAE PSE-TAE vs the E02 baseline and GeoFMs; macro-F1 per seed training curves Ablations each ablation vs the setting it changes one comparison figure each

The Results page collects the one-line answer of every experiment; the RQ1 synthesis (step 6 below) compares the experiments and the two regions.

docs.title: 10. Order of work
docs.text:
One experiment at a time: implement, check on a small run, run in both regions, write the report, then the next.

Step Work Needs 0a ✅ AgriFM normalisation: chip statistics of each region (D15); config statistics as sensitivity run – 0b ✅ Code (13 Nov 2026): region in scripts 02a–05; HGB removed; seeds and label efficiency in 03 / 03b / 03c; new 03c_train_ltae.py; Holm rule in 04; per-region reports; Slurm submitter – 0c ✅ Embeddings, Sentinel-2 only (12 Nov 2026): Morocco TerraMind and AgriFM again, Clay and Prithvi reused; Utah all four (cluster GPU) 0a, 0b 1 E02 Morocco + Utah; report page with tables and figures (make_report.py extended to two regions) 0c 2 Write 03c_train_ltae.py (heads mlp and ltae); E03, then E04; reports 1 3 E05 PSE-TAE (3 seeds) – (can run any time on the cluster) 5 Ablations A1, A4, A2 (A3, A5 if time allows) 1 6 RQ1 synthesis over both regions 1–5

docs.text:
Experiment Runs per region Both regions Hardware E02 5 (× 3 classifiers) 10 CPU, minutes each E03 5 × 3 seeds 30 CPU or GPU, minutes E04 4 × 3 seeds 24 GPU E05 1 × 3 seeds 6 GPU Label efficiency (inside E02–E05) 135 270 CPU (E02) + GPU (E03–E05) Ablations A1, A2, A4 ~15 ~25 CPU (+ GPU for A4 embeddings)

The label-efficiency runs are the largest part; they reuse the code of E02–E05 and only add the training-block subsampling.

docs.title: 12. Open points
docs.text:
• Headline classifier: the protocol keeps random forest for the baseline and the linear probe for the GeoFMs; with SVM the strongest classifier in E01, all three are always reported.
  • Prithvi-EO-2.0 is pretrained on 30 m HLS and applied to 10 m Sentinel-2 (stated as a limitation).
  • Fine-tuning (LoRA, RQ2), the 2024 → 2021 temporal test in Utah (RQ3) and the mapping models follow after RQ1.

docs.title: RQ2 · Fine-tuning and mapping model
docs.text:
Starter page

Design as planned; extended when the work begins (planned November 2026 – January 2027).

Research question RQ2: to what extent does parameter-efficient fine-tuning improve on a frozen encoder?

docs.title: Planned design
docs.text:
The frozen-encoder benchmark of RQ1 pools embeddings over parcel polygons and cannot produce wall-to-wall maps. RQ2 therefore introduces a pixel-level model that serves both as the fine-tuning experiment and as the mapping model of Phase 5 (decision D11).

Component Description Frozen encoder + segmentation head each GeoFM with a UPerNet head trained on the labelled pixels of the tiles, as in PANGAEA and Prithvi-EO-2.0 Parameter-efficient fine-tuning low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of the encoder with the same head Full fine-tuning (optional) all encoder weights trained, for the best model only Classical baseline random forest on the per-pixel Sentinel-1/2 features Neural baselines TempCNN (per-pixel time series) and U-TAE (image time series), trained from scratch

Training, tuning and testing follow the evaluation protocol: the same spatial folds and the PASTIS rotation. Pixel predictions are additionally aggregated to parcels, so that the results are directly comparable with RQ1.

docs.text:
